conviction_note: Mild long lean: the company's own Q3 guide (midpoint +16% y/y) sits well below its Q2 growth (+24%) and fleet growth (+22%), consensus ($346m) sits below the guide midpoint, and the one listed European peer that reported after Lime spoke (Voi, 22 Oct) accelerated to +53%. Against that: a margin-compression trend, a Q4/FY guide that decides the reaction, a stock 42% off its high, and only one prior print to learn the reaction function from. So p_up 56 on an abs move of 12 gives +1.44, slightly below the +1.6 sum of findings. Both numbers point the same way and differ only by the probability tier.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: the company guided $340-360m and adj EBITDA $120-130m in its Q2 8-K of 2026-08-04 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001699963/000114036126031146/ef20079411_ex99-1.htm). Revenue consensus is $346.05m and EPS consensus $0.57 from 3 estimates, both from a single search-summary source (stockanalysis/therighttrader, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/lime/forecast/), so the consensus is single-sourced while the guide is primary. The FY2026 guide is $1.04-1.10B revenue and $265-285m adj EBITDA. FY2025 revenue was $886.7m. Q3 2025 revenue was $301.6m (S-1 via https://micromobility.io/news/886m-230-cities-and-an-ipo-filing---inside-limes-s-1), so the guide implies +12.7% to +19.4% y/y and consensus +14.7%. Implied Q4 2026 is $216-276m against a Q4 2025 of about $210m.
positioning_check: No options market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so there is no skew and no priced direction. Short interest is low: about 1.3m shares, 2.6% of float, 2.9 days to cover in early September 2026 (https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/LIME/). MarketBeat had 723k shares, 1.1% and 1.0 days at the 15 July settlement (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/neutron-holdings-inc-nasdaqlime-short-interest-update-2026-07-29/). Curved Trading lists a 22.4% borrow fee (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lime/). I found no October settlement. This is not a crowded short. Tape: spot $24.945, just under the $25 IPO price, 42% off the 52-week high (~$44.38) and 10% above the low, 20-day run-up -8.8%, 5-day +3.8%, realised vol 86% annualised, 20-day average volume ~353k shares. Sell-side is uniformly bullish (9 Buy, 2 Hold, average target ~$38.9 per MarketBeat 2026-10-19), so the price has fallen well below the analysts' view with no company news. The 160-day lock-up on ~43.1m shares (about 2/3 of the 64m outstanding) expires around 2026-12-07, outside the window.

findings.finding: Lime's own Q3 guide looks conservative against its own run-rate. The $340-360m range implies +12.7% to +19.4% y/y on Q3 2025's $301.6m, midpoint about +16%. Q2 2026 printed +24% ($304.2m vs $246.1m) on a +22% average operational fleet (407,707), and Q1 2026 printed +32%. Consensus at $346m (+14.7%) sits below the guide midpoint. If Q3 simply holds Q2's +24% that is about $374m, roughly 8% over consensus. A second-print IPO beating its own first public guide is the market's expectation for the beat in kind, not necessarily in size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only one prior public print. Q2 2026 (2026-08-04, amc): record revenue +24% with the first Q3/FY guide, and the stock rose +14.54% (baseline). The sweep marks the history untrustworthy as a base rate.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a large beat, the stock would not sit at the IPO price, 42% below the post-Q2 high and below every published target ($33-45). Consensus has not moved off the bottom half of the guide ($346m vs $350m midpoint). The arithmetic is public, but nothing in the price or the estimate shows it was acted on.
findings.independence: Shares its base with the margin finding (same 8-K). The Voi peer print (https://mfn.se/a/voitechnology/voi-technology-ab-publ-publishes-third-quarter-report-2026) and Seattle ridership (GeekWire) are independent and point the same way. Q3 2025 revenue comes from a secondary S-1 summary (micromobility.io); it fits H1 2025 $375.1m and FY2025 $886.7m.

findings.finding: Voi Technology, the largest listed pure-play European peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-22, after Lime last spoke. Net revenue was EUR 88.2m, +53% y/y, accelerating from +47% in Q2 2026. Rides were 53m, against 43m in Q2 (+38% y/y in Q2). Revenue per vehicle per day was EUR 5.36, +10%. Adj EBITDA rose +90%. Voi said Paris regulation was stable with fleets allowed to grow with demand. This points to strong European summer demand and unit economics in Lime's seasonally peak quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of LIME reacting to a peer print. Voi is not exchange-listed equity (bond issuer, VNV Global portfolio company), so its prints are read by few US investors.
findings.why_not_priced: LIME fell through October (-14.7% month to date by 10-27 per AAII; $24.78 on 10-19) after Voi's release, and consensus sits below Lime's guide midpoint. A market reading Voi's acceleration as a Lime read-through would have lifted estimates or the stock. Voi is a Swedish bond-financed private company that US coverage rarely cites.
findings.independence: Proxy: different company, mostly European, and part of its growth is share gain (active vehicles +40% vs Lime fleet +22%), so it can be Voi taking share rather than market growth. Voi Q2 2026 +47% (https://quartr.com/events/voi-technology-voi-q2-2026_F6gi6Vy3) coexisted with Lime Q2 +24%, so the levels do not transfer; only the direction of acceleration does. Seattle ridership (GeekWire) is a separate positive datum.

findings.finding: Lime's Seattle ridership passed 10.5m trips in 2026 by October, above the full-year 2025 total of 9.7m (Lime's own recap), more than two months early. The World Cup alone contributed 1.7m+ trips and a record ~83,000-ride day on 19 June. This is a Lime-sourced city number for one of its larger US markets (about $37.4m of 2025 rental revenue, roughly 4% of company revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; city ridership has never been tied to a LIME print.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (URL path /2026/; the article says 'into October'); snippet_only, because WebFetch returned 403
findings.why_not_priced: City-level ridership is not aggregated by any estimate service, and the October price drift shows no positive read-through.
findings.independence: Segment item, net of the rest: Seattle is about 4% of revenue, and the World Cup trips are split between Q2 (from 11 June) and Q3, so the company-level contribution is a fraction of a point of growth. SDOT reports a 10.5m 2025 figure, against Lime's 9.7m, which would make the 'early' claim weaker (https://sdotblog.seattle.gov/tag/lime/). Independent of the Voi and guide findings.

findings.finding: The quality of the beat is at risk on margins. Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin fell to 52.1% from 55.7% and GAAP gross margin to 42.4% from 44.3%. Operating income fell to $12.8m from $41.5m (SBC $38.1m vs $3m). Free cash flow was -$4.1m vs +$52.3m as vehicle purchases more than doubled ($70.0m vs $31.7m). Q3 adj EBITDA is guided at $120-130m (~36% margin) on a fleet-growth capex year (FY capex ~$180-185m). A revenue beat that comes with further adjusted gross-margin compression, or a FY EBITDA guide that is not raised, could cap the reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2 the stock rose +14.54% despite the 360bp adjusted gross-margin compression and an operating-income decline. On that one print, margins were not punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 42% drawdown since the post-Q2 high may already reflect margin and FCF worries. Consensus EBITDA was not found, so whether the street models compression is unknown.
findings.independence: Same underlying 8-K as the guide finding (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001699963/000114036126031146/ef20079411_ex99-1.htm). It is the counterweight to it, not a contradiction: revenue can beat while margins disappoint. Voi's margin expansion (vehicle-profit margin 65.7% vs 62.9%) points the other way for the industry.

findings.finding: Known capacity losses weigh on Q3 y/y. Denver ended Lime's permit and Lime devices stopped renting after 2026-05-16 (Veo is sole operator). In Paris, Lime cut its e-bike fleet by 30% under the four-year contract that started 2025-10-01 (cap 6,000 per operator). Both were known before the 2026-08-04 Q3 guide and were already in Q2's +24% comp for Paris.
findings.source_date: 2026 (page states Lime/Bird stop renting after 2026-05-16); Paris: https://micromobility.substack.com/p/lime-gears-up-for-paris-renewal-set dated 2025-09-29
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both are inside what the company guided, so sized toward 0. They are filed because they bear on the Q3 comp, and Denver is a full-quarter loss in Q3 for the first time.
findings.independence: Two separate public sources (Denver city page, Denverite 2026-04-15 https://denverite.com/2026/04/15/denver-veo-scooter-contract-moves-forward/; Micromobility newsletter for Paris). Voi's release says Paris fleets may grow with demand, which partly offsets.

findings.finding: After the quarter Lime acquired Neuron Mobility's Canadian operations (Ottawa and cities in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Ontario). The company says this is not material to 2026 revenue, so it touches only the Q4 or FY guide at the margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in August and stated immaterial, so it is close to fully priced; sized near zero.
findings.independence: CTV Ottawa coverage of the Neuron-to-Lime switch (https://www.ctvnews.ca/ottawa/article/scooting-over-neuron-e-scooters-to-be-replaced-by-lime-in-ottawa/).

outside_window.finding: The 160-day IPO lock-up (prospectus dated 2026-06-30) releases about 43.1m shares, roughly two-thirds of 64m outstanding and several times the ~7-8m float, around 2026-12-07. The underwriters (GS, JPM) can release early at their discretion; the 424B4 has no earnings- or price-triggered release. Uber's stake is separately locked for one year. This is an overhang, but it is dated after the window.

baseline_tension: With no option market there is no skew to agree or disagree with; the long lean cuts against the -8.8% 20-day run-up and the 42% drawdown from the high, which could mean disappointment is priced (supporting a beat reaction) or an unseen cause the price knows and the filings do not show.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a proxy loses to a primary number): Voi peer read-through cut from +1.5 to +1.0 and kept as a filed proxy, because part of Voi's growth is share gain and Lime grew half Voi's rate in Q2.

Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction) together with lesson 6 (bar single-sourced on consensus, guide primary): guide-conservatism finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2, and p_up from 57 to 56. Only one prior reaction exists, so a beat being bought is not established.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Seattle ridership cut from +0.6 to +0.4, because Seattle is about 4% of revenue and the World Cup trips are split across Q2 and Q3.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): I left the 42% drawdown with no EDGAR cause unfiled as a finding; it is mentioned only in positioning_check.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct held at 12 rather than shrunk, given an 86% realised vol, a small float and a +14.5% first-print reaction.
Margin, capacity and Neuron findings unchanged.
